raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #35148.

When `qwen3` reasoning parsing is configured only in `sgl-model-gateway`, Qwen3.8 responses can contain a prefilled reasoning segment from the chat template. The gateway parser starts in the wrong state, so the reasoning is returned in `content` and `reasoning_content` remains null instead of separating the thinking and final answer.

## Modifications

- Upgrade `reasoning-parser` from `1.0.0` to `1.3.0`.
- Initialize the non-streaming parser per request, including reset and prefilled-thinking state.
- Initialize each streaming parser per choice with the tokenizer's `ThinkingToggle`, `ThinkingKeyName`, and `think_in_prefill` settings.
- Respect explicit `enable_thinking` / `thinking` request overrides.
- Add unit regressions for Qwen3.8 prefilled `</think>` parsing in streaming and non-streaming paths.

## Accuracy Tests

Added parser unit tests covering:

- Qwen3 prefilled reasoning in the non-streaming path.
- Qwen3 prefilled reasoning and closing `</think>` transition in the streaming path.
- Thinking-toggle defaults and request-key resolution.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This is a reasoning-parser correctness fix and does not change an inference kernel or performance-critical model computation.

Hi @CatherineSue @key4ng @slin1237,

When you have a chance, could you please review this PR? Any feedback would be greatly appreciated. Thank you very much for your time!

Was looking at my upstream issue and noticed two PRs for this, just wanted to cross link them here for reference in the event the maintainers may not notice:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35346

Hi @CatherineSue @key4ng @slin1237,

There has been no formal review activity on this PR for some time, so we wanted to check whether this change is still relevant and whether we should continue working on it. We understand priorities can change; if the issue is already covered elsewhere or the scope should be adjusted, please let us know and we will follow your guidance.

If the PR is still useful, could you please take a look when you have time? Feedback on the implementation, tests, or whether the branch should be updated would be very helpful. We hope to contribute in a way that helps move the SGLang project forward.

Thank you very much for your time.

Thanks @ActiveSky. Closing this because you have 13 PRs open and none updated in 7 days, over our soft cap of 5 for idle PRs.

Reopen the two or three you most want reviewed - a short active set moves faster than a long idle one.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

Got to love this kind of response to close our PRs that are actively requesting some kind of review, but your only allowed to have so many active PRs at any given time... which somehow will make it "faster" to review despite the fact that this has sat idel for months.

Let alone the comment about how directories and files have changed relating around python code when this PR addresses issues in the Rust implementation of the sgl-model-gateway and not sgl-kernel nor python.
